anonymous_statement.{u_1} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (j : ℕ)
  (w : E) :
  ↑↑(anonymous_object_1 j
          w) =ᵐ[ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E]
    fun x => (Polynomial.aeval (Inner.inner ℝ w x)) (Polynomial.hermite j)

blind_reconstruction.text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm and Borel sigma-algebra. Let gamma_E be the centered Gaussian probability measure on E with covariance the identity. Let L^2(gamma_E; R) be the real Hilbert space of square-integrable real-valued functions modulo gamma_E-almost-everywhere equality. Write H_j for the unnormalized probabilists' Hermite polynomial of degree j, with its integer coefficients interpreted in R (H_0(t)=1, H_1(t)=t, and H_(n+1)(t)=t H_n(t)-n H_(n-1)(t) for n>=1). Define Phi_j(w)=[x |-> H_j(<w,x>)] in L^2(gamma_E; R), where brackets denote the almost-everywhere equivalence class of the literal square-integrable function displayed. For every j in N={0,1,2,...} and every w in E, let r_(j,w):E -> R be the representative function obtained by coercing Phi_j(w) from L^2 through its almost-everywhere-function class to a function. Then r_(j,w)(x)=H_j(<w,x>) for gamma_E-almost every x in E. On the right, the integer-coefficient Hermite polynomial is evaluated in R using the canonical integer-to-real algebra map. The almost-everywhere quantifier lies inside the quantifiers over j and w; the assertion does not require a common exceptional null set for all w, and it does not assert equality at every x.
